stem: A three-tier application's NAT gateway needs to sit somewhere it can actually reach the internet so the private tiers behind it get outbound access, and a metro-area gaming audience needs compute placed closer than the parent Region can reach. Select TWO placements that meet these two requirements. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Place the NAT gateway in a public subnet with a route to an internet gateway
Extend the workload into a Wavelength Zone embedded in a telecom carrier's 5G network for the gaming audience
Place the NAT gateway in the same private subnet as the tiers it serves
Provision a Direct Connect connection to reach the metro-area gaming audience directly
Extend the workload into a Local Zone connected to its parent Region for the gaming audience

rationale: A NAT gateway only has somewhere to send internet-bound traffic if it sits in a public subnet with its own route to an internet gateway; that placement is what lets it forward the private tiers' outbound connections. A Local Zone extends the parent Region to a location closer to a metro-area audience, which fits a general gaming audience with no stated carrier-network requirement. Placing the NAT gateway in the same private subnet as the tiers it serves leaves it without a route to an internet gateway itself, so it has no internet path to forward traffic to. A Wavelength Zone is built for workloads embedded inside a telecom carrier's own network; nothing in the scenario ties the gaming audience to a specific carrier's 5G network, so a Local Zone fits better. Direct Connect links an on-premises network to AWS; it is not a way to reach a general public gaming audience.
